idiom_name: interface methods lock, implementation methods assume the lock is held
implementation_notes: Split every operation into an interface method that acquires the component's lock at the border and an implementation method that assumes the lock is held and touches the guarded state directly. The implementation family never acquires or releases the lock and never calls an interface method, so an intra-component call graph stays inside one critical section. Acquire through a scope-bound guard so every exit path releases, name the implementation family consistently and state 'the caller must hold the lock' where the helpers are defined. Because the component never relies on re-entrancy, the same structure runs on a non-recursive mutex, a recursive mutex (paying overhead it does not need) or a Null Mutex.
code_sketch:
find(key):                        # interface method: acquires once
    guard(lock)
    return find_impl(key)

find_impl(key):                   # implementation method: lock already held
    entry = lookup_impl(key)
    if entry is missing:
        entry = bind_impl(key)    # safe: no re-acquisition
    return entry
pitfalls: Calling an interface method from an implementation method re-acquires the lock: an instant self-deadlock on a non-recursive mutex, silent overhead on a recursive one.
The 'lock is held' precondition is unchecked: a subclass, friend, test or callback that calls an implementation method directly causes a data race nothing reports.
Callbacks, listeners and virtual calls made while holding the lock can re-enter the component from outside and deadlock on the same lock.

Maintenance drift in the other direction: a newly added public method that calls implementation methods but forgets to acquire the lock at the border exposes the guarded state without protection - a silent data race no test reliably catches.

Escaping to a recursive mutex to make a self-call work and then waiting on a condition variable: POSIX warns the implicit unlock in pthread_cond_wait may not release a mutex locked more than once, so the predicate can never be satisfied by other threads.
